data.title: Incremental projection, so a write refreshes the snapshot
data.description: The second half of KAD-45, split out because it is not a small change. A write appends an event and leaves the snapshot stale, so the next read pays a full journal read: 566 ms at 10k events, measured end to end after KAD-45. Rebuilding eagerly after a write is not the fix - it moves the cost from the read to the write and makes a write-heavy loop worse. The fix is an apply(state, event) that is provably equivalent to a full fold. project() is not a left fold: phase one seeds every entity up front because an entity can merge after the events that refer to it (I2, ADR-013), documents fold after the loop from a revision list the state does not carry, and labels are assigned during folding. I1 is at stake, so equivalence needs to be tested against project() over the same events in shuffled read orders, not asserted.
